specs.value: Hang-on-back (lọc thác/lọc treo) power filter with a self-priming pump
130–450 US GPH (500–2000 L/H), depending on model
Adjustable, e.g. Tidal 110 goes from about 450 down to 90 GPH
Self-cleaning and corrosion-resistant, on a shaft made of corrosion-resistant metal; for freshwater and saltwater
3 years against material and workmanship defects (impeller excluded), extended to 5 years if registered
3 years with a warranty card, from the official Seachem Vietnam distributor
No dual intake, no telescoping intake, no heater holder

prices.variant: Tidal 75 (out of stock; the description says 1,200k)
Tidal 110 (price only in the description; out of stock)

fits.fact: Works in both freshwater and saltwater tanks thanks to the corrosion-resistant impeller
The Tidal 35 suits tanks of about 130 L; the 55, 75 and 110 suit about 200, 300 and 400 L
Needs 7–9.5 cm of space behind the tank, depending on model, so check the gap to the wall
The basket is open, so the whole interior can hold whatever media you choose; it could even work as a media reactor in a reef tank
Vietnamese shops say each unit comes with Seachem Matrix biomedia and a sponge
A user worried that very small fish such as neons could get pulled into the Tidal 110's intake slots, so a prefilter sponge is sensible for small fish or shrimp
Tanks covered with floating plants such as duckweed can clog the surface skimmer

usage.fact: The pump primes itself: you don't need to fill the basket or start a siphon, and it restarts on its own after a power cut
Keep the water above the minimum line marked on the filter, or the pump will stop
A leveling dial lets you set the filter level on uneven tank rims
When the media clogs, water goes out a side outlet and a blue indicator rises on top, which tells you it's time to clean
The 55, 75 and 110 have a telescoping intake and adjustable surface/sub-surface intake; you can change the intake depth without turning the filter off
The basket lifts out without dripping, which makes rinsing the media easier
If the filter stops: unplug it, take out the pump and impeller, and rinse both; keep the original impeller for any warranty claim
Clean the prefilter sponge and impeller often; a dirty sponge or impeller is a common cause of noise

issues.fact: Some owners report impeller rattling; one fixed it by lightly sanding the impeller, and another by cleaning the impeller and filter
Some Tidal 110 owners stayed noisy even after a warranty motor and impeller replacement or silicone lubrication
On one Tidal 75, the skimmer kept sucking in duckweed and blocking the filter every few minutes
Others report their Tidal 75s running quietly with little maintenance for more than a year
Seachem's support page says the impeller is only covered for 6 months, unlike the 3-year warranty on the rest of the filter
Version differences: the Tidal 35 lacks the dual intake, telescoping intake and heater holder that the larger models have
Some Vietnamese shop pages list incorrect specs (for example, Tidal 35 at 1300 L/h or Tidal 110 at 4000 L/h/16 W); trust Seachem's figures instead

alternatives.why: A classic hang-on filter with a large media basket and easy-to-find spare parts. It's often cheaper but needs priming, and it has no surface skimmer or clog indicator.
Made in the same Sicce factory with the same design. It may cost differently depending on the distributor in Vietnam.
Much cheaper and easy to find in Vietnam, for those on a budget, though build quality and quietness are weaker than the Tidal.
